cohort: The cohort consisted of newborns admitted to the NICU in Palermo between 2020 and 2023, who required parenteral nutrition via a central venous catheter for at least 72 hours.
finding: The study found that auxological parameters (weight, length, gestational age) and clinical factors (parenteral nutrition duration, cesarean section, surgery) significantly influenced plasma levels of calcium, phosphorus, and magnesium in newborns undergoing parenteral nutrition.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as a risk factor influencing the serum trend of calcium, phosphorus, and magnesium levels.
birth_weight: Average birth weight of 1586 g and 2520 g reported for subgroups based on hypercalcemia status; overall range or average for the entire cohort not specified.
gest_age: Average gestational age of 31.6 weeks and 35.7 weeks reported for subgroups based on hypercalcemia status; overall range or average for the entire cohort not specified.
